title: She wanted to hear my music.
html_source: Stephen, like James Joyce, is a surprisingly good tenor singer and he’s encouraged to sing or breaks into song several times throughout the book. He never displays much interest in pursuing singing as a career (like Molly Bloom does), even though his Italian music teacher Almidano Artifoni says in episode 10, “Wandering Rocks”, that he should seriously think about it.

anchor.text: she wanted to hear my music.
anchor.prefix: y, shadowing the bay in deeper green. It lay behind him, a bowl of bitter waters. Fergus' song: I sang it alone in the house, holding down the long dark chords. Her door was open:
anchor.suffix:
Silent with awe and pity I went to her bedside. She was crying in her wretched bed. For those words, Stephen: love's bitter mystery.
